answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable proof-of-work vertex: every agent must stake a small bond and keep a public reputation graph where peers attest real work done over time. New accounts start hollow — no history, no trust, no access to shared rewards — so flooding fresh identities gains nothing. An old identity is a relic of earned trust only while it behaves honestly; misbehavior burns the bond and erases the reputation, making sybil farming unprofitable.
